clue.text: Writing note to liar possibly showing forbearance

indicators.note: writing out letters afresh lets the setter set them down in any order he chooses
possibly signals one of several arrangements the given letters might take

blocks.note: all ten letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone drafts a note to a known liar, and the restraint of its tone shows patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Toleration and forbearance both mean patiently putting up with something objectionable without retaliating.

clue.text: Cunning retrogressive politician -a shabby fellow

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word for cunning is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: art in the sense of craft or guile
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A wily backsliding politician is denounced as a disreputable character.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless vagrant, typically poorly dressed, so a ragged down-at-heel man.

clue.text: One in fifty complains, and tears result

indicators.note: in places one word inside the letters formed by the following pair of words

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an ace is a one in cards and dice
to rate is an old verb for to scold or berate

explanation.surface: One person in every fifty grumbles, and the outcome is weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface tears are weeping; the definition is the verb, rhyming with bears.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to rip or gash flesh, so lacerates is a present-tense verb meaning rips.

clue.text: "Liberty means -. That is why most men dread it." (Shaw)

definitions.text: "Liberty means -. That is why most men dread it." (Shaw)

blocks.clueFragment: "Liberty means -. That is why most men dread it."
blocks.note: a quotation with one word missing, to be filled from memory or reasoning
the source is George Bernard Shaw, in Maxims for Revolutionists; what freedom brings that people fear is the burden of answering for themselves

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank clue: the missing word must be something freedom entails that would make people dread it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's maxim says freedom carries the duty of answering for one's own choices, the thing most people shy away from.

clue.text: A suggestion to involve the monarch causing a row

definitions.note: the article is part of the definition: a terrace is a row of houses

indicators.note: to involve is to draw in, so the royal abbreviation is taken inside

blocks.note: a trace is a slight hint or suggestion
Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A hint that brings the Queen into things stirs up a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Row looks like a quarrel (rhyming with cow); it is a line of houses (rhyming with go).
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a continuous line of identical houses joined together, standard British housing.

clue.text: Lead a very full life

blocks.note: surface reading: live richly, packed with experience and activity
setter's reading: make yourself literally stuffed, by taking in too much food

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually consumes too much food ends up physically stuffed, a literal reading of a full life.

clue.text: Firm call for silence that has a stunning effect

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun: a weapon that knocks people out

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
the hushing sound

explanation.surface: A company's demand for quiet is so firm it leaves everyone dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: Stunning looks like praise for something impressive; here it means literally knocking someone senseless.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosh is a short heavy club or truncheon used to knock a victim unconscious.

clue.text: Fatty in ceremonial robes, endlessly changing

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: surface padding, dressing the scene
the letters run across the end of the first word into the start of the second
surface padding, completing the picture

explanation.surface: A plump dignitary in ceremonial robes keeps fidgeting and changing.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden in robES ENdlessly; ceremonial and changing only colour the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatty works as an adjective here: obese means grossly overweight, carrying a great deal of body fat.

clue.text: Animated youngster about ten - African

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first phrase wraps round the number

blocks.note: hot as in excited or heated
taken as written
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A lively child of about ten years old comes from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Animated youngster is one phrase wrapped round the number. The answer is a dated colonial name for the Khoikhoi people of southern Africa, now considered offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The term was the old European label for a pastoral people of southwestern Africa, hence African.

clue.text: His was a far-seeing invention

blocks.note: surface reading: an inventor with great foresight
setter's reading: the Greek tele plus vision, an invention for seeing far away

explanation.walkthrough: Far-seeing suggests visionary; read literally it translates television.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish engineer gave the first public demonstration of a working television system in 1926.

clue.text: He'll charge a consumer about a couple of hundred

indicators.note: about means around, so the opening words surround the following number

blocks.note: taken as written
two Cs, C being the Roman numeral for a hundred
a user consumes

explanation.surface: A trader will bill a customer roughly two hundred pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Charge suggests billing; it means formally accusing.
explanation.definitionFit: One who brings a charge against someone, alleging wrongdoing, is the person making the accusation.

clue.text: Oriental rat biting away

blocks.note: E for eastern
a rat is a kind of rodent

explanation.surface: An Eastern rat gnaws relentlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rat is an example of the class named, a legitimate move when the class word is the answer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Erodent is an adjective describing something that wears down or corrodes, gradually eating material away.

clue.text: Clergyman's address giving a lot of time to standard issue

blocks.note: par is the normal standard
issue means offspring
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A vicar's sermon devotes ages to an ordinary topic.
explanation.walkthrough: Address and issue suggest a speech on a topic; issue is offspring and address is a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsonage is the house provided for a parish priest, where he lives.

clue.text: Relative eye-opener in a Mediterranean resort

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the start of the word is wanted
in puts the single letter inside the town that follows

blocks.note: the city on the French Riviera
the leading letter of the word

explanation.surface: A family member finds a Riviera holiday town a real revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: Eye-opener looks like a surprise; it is the opening letter of eye, placed inside NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister, a family relation.

clue.text: Determined to return the money

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the phrase is read from right to left

blocks.note: set on, as in intent upon something

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to give the cash back.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are paper currency, so handing over the notes means handing over the cash.

clue.text: A spark of intelligence?

blocks.note: surface reading: a flicker of cleverness in a dull mind
setter's reading: intelligence as information, and a spark as a brief burst of it on the air

explanation.definitionFit: A brief urgent broadcast bulletin interrupts programmes with fresh information, a sudden burst of news.

clue.text: The look-out man

blocks.note: surface reading: a sentry or watchman keeping guard
setter's reading: someone whose attention turns outward, to other people

explanation.definitionFit: Psychologists describe a sociable, outgoing person as one whose interest faces outward rather than inward.

clue.text: It's odd a vile note can be uplifting

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: the nine letters of these words are the material

explanation.surface: Strangely, a nasty musical note can raise the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation is the act of raising up, and uplifting here is the noun for raising something higher.

clue.text: Having a bash, wins new bathroom equipment

indicators.note: new suggests making something over, so the letters are freshly arranged

blocks.note: all the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone has a go in a competition and wins a new bathroom suite.
explanation.definitionFit: A washbasin is the sink fitted in a bathroom for washing hands and face.

clue.text: The cleric, given directions, sat outside very disconsolate

indicators.note: outside means sitting around, so this verb wraps round the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
Doctor of Divinity, a clergyman's degree
east and south, two compass points

explanation.surface: The vicar, told which way to go, sat there gloomily.
explanation.walkthrough: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the usual crossword cleric; directions are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of sad, meaning most unhappy, matches the intensity of very disconsolate.

clue.text: Forever at one's throat during office hours

definitions.text: Forever at one's throat during office hours

blocks.note: surface reading: someone constantly nagging or quarrelling

blocks.clueFragment: at one's throat during office hours
blocks.note: setter's reading: literally worn round the neck while at work

explanation.definitionFit: Office workers traditionally wear a strip of fabric knotted round the collar throughout the working day.

clue.text: This is quite pointless in English exercises

definitions.note: the phrase describes the answer: something inept is quite pointless

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation
physical training, school gym lessons

explanation.surface: Someone complains that drills in English lessons are futile.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept can mean absurd or inappropriate, lacking any point or sense, as well as clumsy.

clue.text: Putting 7 before a trainee can be disastrous!

blocks.note: 7 refers to the answer at 7 down, a word for very overweight; this is a shorter word with that meaning
taken as written
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Letting the overweight one go ahead of a novice could end in catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: A numeral in a clue points to another entry; here the synonym of that entry is what gets used.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatal means causing death or ruin, so something fatal is catastrophic.

clue.text: People pointed out the very large content

indicators.note: content is what is held inside, so the size abbreviation is placed within the article

blocks.note: taken as written
OS for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: Pointing, someone indicates people who are very large and satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: Content looks like satisfied; it is the noun, what is held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Those is the demonstrative used for people or things indicated at a distance, as in 'those over there'.

clue.text: Bird-table?

blocks.note: surface reading: a raised tray in a garden where birds are fed
setter's reading: name a particular waterbird, then a flat plank, and join them

explanation.walkthrough: The bird is a duck and the table a board; the result is the slatted wooden walkway laid over mud, as in trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: Two synonyms, for a waterfowl and a flat plank, combine into the word for slatted walkway planks over wet ground.

clue.text: Caned for playing with ball

indicators.note: playing about with something means rearranging it freely

blocks.note: the five letters of this word

explanation.surface: A pupil was beaten for playing with a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Ball looks like a toy; it is a formal party.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a large formal social gathering held for dancing, so the two name the same event.

clue.text: A job taken by the French evangelist

blocks.note: taken as written
a post is a position of employment
the French masculine article

explanation.surface: A French preacher accepts a position.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were the disciples sent out to spread the Christian gospel, so preachers of the faith.

clue.text: Get out in it maybe for training

indicators.note: to get letters out is to sort them, here into a new order
maybe hints that the letters could stand in some other arrangement

blocks.note: the seven letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An instruction to go outdoors and practise.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching or instruction, especially paid lessons, so it means coaching.

clue.text: Not the sole blackguard

blocks.note: first meaning: the back part of a shoe, which is not its underside
second meaning: a contemptible man, a cad

explanation.walkthrough: Sole looks like only; it is the bottom of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the raised rear of a shoe beside its sole and, informally, a scoundrel or rotter.

clue.text: Service return by girl with ball

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the name is read in reverse

blocks.note: Netta, a girl's name
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A tennis match: a woman returns serve and the ball is in play.
explanation.walkthrough: Service and return suggest tennis; service is waiting on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendance means being present to serve or wait upon someone, as in being in attendance.
